title: Convergent deployment policy adapter for isolated inference zones
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem statement: We need a single declarative surface that lets teams express canary/A-B/shadowing/rollback experiments at a high-level while ensuring deterministic, safe execution across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Current issues: (1) policy primitives diverge per environment (Hosted supports traffic-splits + auto-fallback; Dedicated supports capacity reservations but different network constraints; Private often lacks runtime autoscaler and has stricter upgrade windows), (2) teams duplicate rollout recipes per environment, and (3) safety behaviors (auto-rollback triggers, admission fencing) are implemented at different layers leading to race conditions during cross-environment promotion.

Goal: Implement a Convergent Deployment Policy Adapter (CDPA) that compiles a single high-level rollout spec into an environment-specific execution plan with environment-aware guards and a unified observation surface for rollback decisions. The adapter should: compile policy -> execution plan, inject environment safety fences (capacity checks, maintenance windows, KMS access verification), orchestrate staged activation (transactional activation semantics to avoid split-model serving within a host), and surface unified telemetry to the Console for canary metrics and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Teams can submit a single 'cdpa' rollout spec and target any combination of Hosted/Dedicated/Private and observe consistent behavior in a staged test cluster.

2) The CDPA emits an execution plan that maps high-level knobs (percent, shadow_ratio, evaluation_window, rollback_signal_def) to environment primitives; we have unit tests verifying mapping for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

3) Auto-rollback can be exercised with synthetic signals: when evaluation_window reports error_rate > threshold or quality_regression delta > configured tolerance, CDPA triggers a rollback action within 60s in Hosted and within the documented SLA for Dedicated/Private with a clear state transition visible in Console.

4) Private environment safety fence supports scheduled maintenance windows and operator approval gate; attempt to run a disruptive promotion during a blocked window should be rejected with a clear error code.
5) Shadow traffic can be enabled with soft isolation: shadowed requests do not consume production KV cache unless explicitly opted in, and cost accounting is attributed separately in telemetry.
6) Documentation and sample specs for 3 canonical patterns (simple canary, A/B with multi-metric judge, read-only shadow test) exist in the repo and are linked from the Console rollout wizard.
7) Security review checklist completed and signed off for Private KMS/HSM key usage and console access patterns.
implementation_notes: Architecture: CDPA = declarative parser + policy normalizer + environment compiler + executor agent. Keep compiler deterministic to allow dry-run and plan-inspect in Console CLI.

Execution model: two-phase activation. Phase A: dry-run and capacity precheck; Phase B: transactional route flip with heartbeat and immutable activation token to avoid partial activation across replica sets.
Rollback signals: combine model-quality (eval metrics), infra-health (latency/p95, OOM), and cost anomalies (sudden token bill spikes) using a weighted decision engine configurable per rollout.

Private environment constraints: assume no central autoscaler; provide a 'node-reservation' primitive that translates to ops runbook or agent-based reservation API. If reservation cannot be satisfied, mark plan as BLOCKED and present operator actions.

Telemetry: emit unified rollout_id and per-environment plan_id. Implement a Prometheus->Console adapter for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private provide a lightweight metrics forwarder shim that can be installed as an optional component.
Compatibility: maintain backward-compatible flags for legacy rollout specs while making new 'cdpa/v1' the canonical API.
runbook: 1) Start with dry-run: `redwood rollout plan --spec myrollout.yaml --env hosted --dry-run` to inspect compiled plan.
2) Validate capacity: CDPA runs prechecks and emits `capacity_ok=true|false` and recommended mitigation steps.
3) Approval: For Private, require operator approval token unless `auto_approve_private=true` is set by enterprise contracts.
4) Activate: CDPA initiates transactional activation; monitor Console rollout timeline for successful heartbeats from each zone.
5) If rollback condition met: CDPA triggers an environment-appropriate rollback primitive and annotates the endpoint and model version in audit logs.
6) If rollback failed in Private (e.g., operator unreachable), CDPA escalates to on-call and creates a rollback SOP incident linking to the runbook.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Implementing transactional activation increases complexity of the serving runtime; tradeoff is stronger guarantees vs longer activation latency (expected +3s median).
Tight coupling to Private operator workflows reduces automation but is necessary for safety in regulated environments; mitigation: provide opt-in automation where contracts allow.
A unified decision engine risks overfitting to Hosted telemetry signals; mitigations: make signal weights configurable per environment and allow environment-specific override blocks.
